inputs.notes: Routed per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md: 'Insurer, holdco, compounder-of-book -> BVPS compounding x exit P/B'. Chubb is a genuine book-value compounder (unlike IAG.AX, which was overridden to FCFE-at-CoE because IAG pays out 60-80% of earnings and does not compound book) -- Chubb retains ~85% of core operating earnings (FY2024/FY2025 payout ratios 15.6%/14.7%), buys back ~1.7%/yr of shares, and management explicitly guides to 'sustainable double-digit' EPS and tangible-book-value-per-share growth plus 14%+ core operating ROE / 20%+ ROTE (Q2 2026 earnings). Owner-FCF DCF is NOT used: OCF/FCF for an insurer commingles float movements and investment-portfolio purchases with true distributable cash and is not a clean per-share compounding signal. First research pass on this ticker; no prior DCF or MEMORY.md entry exists (fresh build).
inputs.buyback_pace_note: Shares fell 408.5m (FY2024) -> 401.5m (FY2025) -> 394.6m (Q1 2026), ~1.7%/yr; new $7.5bn buyback authorization effective 2026-07-01 supplements a 30+ year consecutive dividend-growth streak.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity used directly (dividend-discount / BVPS-compounding model, not WACC on a levered FCF stream -- net debt is held at zero per the routing rule for capitalization-style insurer models). Base case CoE 9.0% (risk-free ~4.2% 10yr UST + ERP ~5% for a moderately-levered, moderately cyclical global P&C/life insurer with reserve and catastrophe risk); bull 8.5% (diversification and underwriting discipline reduce risk); bear 9.5% (softening pricing cycle, reserve/social-inflation risk, cat volatility).
inputs.lease_treatment: not applicable (insurer, not an owner-FCF operating-lease model)
inputs.nci_treatment: Huatai Insurance Group (China) is majority-owned/consolidated; reported shareholders' equity is already net of the NCI share per GAAP consolidation, so no further NCI deduction applied.
inputs.data_gap_note: DividendPerShare is missing in CB_Metrics.csv for FY2016-FY2021 (spans the 2016 ACE/Chubb merger share-count reset from ~339m to ~466m shares). Not fabricated; the historical growth CAGRs below use only years with clean equity/share and EPS data, and the projection is anchored to management's current guidance and the post-merger FY2022-FY2025 + Q1 2026 actuals rather than a spliced pre/post-merger DPS series.

historical_growth.bvps_3yr_note: 3yr CAGR (FY2022-FY2025) is inflated by a depressed FY2022 base: shareholders' equity fell to $50.5bn (BVPS $119.28) on unrealized AOCI mark-to-market bond losses from the 2022 rate shock, not an operating deterioration. Not used as the primary anchor.
historical_growth.total_value_creation_note: BVPS growth plus dividends paid, FY2022->FY2025; same FY2022-trough distortion as above.
historical_growth.eps_cagr_note: EPS series is not comparable across the FY2016 ACE/Chubb merger (share count jumped ~37%) or across FY2020-2022 (COVID + reserve/AOCI noise), so EPS CAGR is not used as the primary selector.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management guidance (sustainable double-digit EPS/TBV growth, 14%+ core operating ROE) cross-checked against ROE x retention = 14.5% x (1-15%) = 12.3% sustainable BVPS growth -- used as the base-case anchor in place of a raw historical CAGR, because both 5yr and 10yr BVPS CAGRs are compressed by AOCI/rate-cycle noise unrelated to underwriting economics, and 3yr is inflated by the FY2022 trough base.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 5yr BVPS CAGR (8.7%) vs the ROE x retention sustainable rate (12.3%) diverge by more than 30%; the gap is attributed to two large AOCI swings (2022 losses, partial 2023-2025 recovery) rather than a change in underlying earnings power, and is called out here per the CAGR-divergence check rather than silently resolved.

base.narrative: Base case tracks management's own 'sustainable double-digit' EPS/TBV guidance and current 14.5% core operating ROE, tapering modestly in years 4-5 as the commercial P&C and reinsurance pricing cycle continues to soften per the Analysis JSON's industry-outlook read. Exit P/B of 1.55x sits just below the current 1.65x multiple, reflecting a normal cyclical de-rating as growth decelerates, not a franchise-quality concern.

bull.narrative: Worksite Benefits and Huatai Life continue at their current double-digit-to-high-20s% growth rates, private/alternative asset allocation lifts net investment income faster than the base case, and underwriting discipline holds combined ratios in the low 80s even as peers loosen. Larger buyback pace funded by the new $7.5bn authorization plus continued reserve releases. Exit multiple re-rates toward the top of Chubb's historical range on sustained ROE outperformance.

bear.narrative: Commercial P&C and global reinsurance pricing softens harder than expected (property rates down double digits on some placements per the Analysis JSON), a period of adverse casualty reserve development materializes from social inflation/nuclear verdicts, and one or more above-average catastrophe years (echoing the ~$1.5bn Q1 2025 LA wildfire hit) recur. Buyback pace slows to preserve capital. Exit multiple compresses toward the low end of Chubb's historical 1.1-1.3x range in a de-rated, harder-market environment.

scenario_narratives.base: Management's own guidance (double-digit EPS/TBV growth, 14%+ ROE) continues to be delivered through a softening but not broken P&C pricing cycle, with life/A&H (Huatai, Worksite Benefits) and rising net investment income offsetting flat-to-down commercial property pricing.
scenario_narratives.bull: The diversification thesis plays out fully: Asia life/A&H and high-net-worth personal lines keep compounding at 15-29%, disciplined underwriting holds combined ratios in the low 80s through the soft market, and the $7.5bn buyback authorization is deployed aggressively, all while ROE holds above 15%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The P&C/reinsurance pricing cycle turns harder than management expects, casualty reserves face an adverse development cycle from social inflation, and catastrophe losses recur at an above-average pace, compressing both growth and the exit multiple.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 25/50/25. Not skewed toward bear despite softening-cycle risk: Chubb's diversification (life/A&H, personal lines, reinsurance) and disciplined underwriting culture are structural strengths documented across a full cycle, not a one-off tailwind, and the balance sheet carries no refinancing or solvency risk (debt/equity ~0.31x, modest leverage per the Analysis JSON's own risk section). Not skewed toward bull either: the pricing cycle has genuinely turned, and reserve/catastrophe risk is real and recurring, not merely a tail scenario.
probability_weighted.band_position_note: House and street bases coincide for this model (no SBC add-back applies to a BVPS-compounding valuation); band_position is not meaningful and is reported null rather than a misleading 0/100.

sensitivity.sensitivity_note: Rows = exit P/B multiple (1.25x-1.85x), columns = cost of equity (7%-11%), base-case BVPS growth/payout/buyback path held constant. Current P/B = current_price / inputs.book_value_per_share (see those fields for the live figures).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Chubb is valued as a book-value compounder, not an owner-FCF operating company: shareholders' equity per share is projected forward using management's own guided ROE and retention rate (ROE x (1-payout) = sustainable BVPS growth), dividends along the path are discounted at the cost of equity, and a terminal value is set by capitalizing the Year-5 BVPS at an exit price-to-book multiple consistent with Chubb's historical trading range (roughly 1.1x-1.85x book across cycles). Net debt is held at zero throughout -- for an insurer, financial leverage funds the investment portfolio backing policy liabilities, not operating assets, and subtracting it would double-count financing cost already embedded in the ROE used to project book value.
key_risks_to_valuation: Casualty reserve adequacy: social inflation and nuclear jury verdicts could force adverse reserve development that reduces reported ROE and BVPS growth below the projected path

Catastrophe loss volatility: a repeat or worsening of events like the January 2025 LA wildfires (~$1.5bn pre-tax hit) would depress a single year's BVPS growth and could trigger reinsurance market hardening

Softening P&C/reinsurance pricing cycle: if commercial property and casualty pricing falls faster or further than assumed, premium growth and underwriting margin both compress, pulling the realized path toward or below the bear case

Exit multiple compression: a de-rating of the whole P&C sector (not specific to Chubb) would reduce the terminal value regardless of BVPS execution, since ~90%+ of the intrinsic value in every scenario comes from the terminal P/B capitalization rather than the interim dividend stream
China/Huatai regulatory risk: majority ownership of a Chinese financial-services group exposes the growth thesis to regulatory and geopolitical risk largely outside management's control

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
